question_text: Founded in 1891 in Chicago, the company began by selling soap and used free baking powder to boost sales during early promotions. When the premium outperformed soap, it pivoted to baking powder. Again, as part of a promotion, they offered two packs of ______ ____ with each purchase as an incentive. The freebie won again, so the company made it the core business, expanding distribution and advertising nationwide. Today, it is the largest manufacturer and marketer of this product across multiple continents. ID the brand.

X is a thick, spiced flatbread with an almost biscuit-like texture and a hard crust. Part of Mughlai cuisine, the bread is made with flour, semolina, ghee, sugar, and saffron-tinged molasses, often speckled with poppy or nigella seeds. A popular legend links its name to a tragic tale of Mirza Agha _____, a general under Siraj-ud-Daulah, and _____ Begum, a dancer. As a tribute to their doomed romance, the bread was christened with a compound of their names. ID this bread which is popular in regions of India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, and Russia.

For the third episode of season 22 of The Simpsons, titled "MoneyBart", the couch gag was created by the artist X, marking it the first time that an artist had been invited to storyboard the show. In the couch gag, after the Simpsons settle on the couch, the camera cuts to an "Asian sweatshop" where artists toil amid bones and waste. A child washes cells in biohazard fluid; kittens are mulched to stuff Bart dolls; a panda hauls toys; a dolphin's tongue seals boxes; and a unicorn's horn punches DVD holes. The camera reveals the factory inside a 20th Century Fox logo, playing on TV. ID the artist X who storyboarded this sequence.

X is an Indian documentary filmmaker known for his socio-political, human rights-oriented films. His films are known to explore themes such as the rise of religious fundamentalism, sectarianism and casteism in India, nuclear nationalism, and unsustainable development. Virtually all of X's films have faced censorship from the Indian government, eventually being cleared after legal action. Upon being asked in a BFI interview to deliver a message for future documentary filmmakers, X famously replied: "No message really. Do it only if it burns when you don't." ID X.

X (three-word title) is an opera in three acts by John Adams with a libretto by Alice Goodman. The intriguing subject of the opera was seen by the makers as both "a ridiculously cynical election ploy ... and a historical breakthrough". Rather than being a satire and poking fun at the two central figures on whom the opera is based, the opera is "heroic in nature". As Adams worked on the opera, he began to see the "American", whom he had once intensely disliked, as an "interesting character", a complicated individual who sometimes showed emotion in public. For the "foreigner", Adams wanted him to be "the ____ of the huge posters and Great Leap Forward". ID the title/subjects of the opera.

X was a Canadian stand-up comedian, who has appeared in numerous films and was a frequent guest on late-night talk shows. X was a cast member on SNL from 1993 to 1998, and also had hosting duties for the 'Weekend Update' segment of the show. In 1998, he was fired from the show for, allegedly, relentlessly mocking O. J. Simpson during his murder trial. A year and a half after his firing, X returned to SNL as a guest host. In his monologue, X hilariously brought up his firing, humorously questioning how he could be funny enough to host, but not funny enough to be on the show. ID X.

The origin of the word X lie in John Milton's epic poem, Paradise Lost. It was used to refer to the capital of hell, where Satan and his peers gathered. In modern usage, X refers to a situation where all hell breaks loose. X is also the title of the season finale of the third season of The Good Place. In the episode, Eleanor asks Janet the meaning of existence; Janet responds that love between humans is special because the "X" of the Universe cannot be understood. ID X.

In Roman mythology, X is the god of beginnings, gates, transitions, time, duality, doorways, passages, frames, and endings. He is usually depicted as having a double-sided head. In the 1995 James Bond movie, GoldenEye, the main antagonist calls himself by the code name X, after he betrays Bond and MI6. After learning of the betrayal, Bond remarks, "Hence, X. The two-faced Roman god come to life". X is also the name of a programming language, so named because every logical variable in it has as its two "faces", two aspects that can be passed as arguments. ID X.

X (four-word phrase) is an adage of Persian origin, known in the Western world primarily due to a 19th-century retelling of a Persian fable by the English poet Edward FitzGerald, titled 'Solomon's Seal': "The Sultan asked Solomon for a Signet motto, that should hold good for Adversity or Prosperity. Solomon gave him, X" ID X that received renewed attention when a cricketer shared it as a message on Twitter/X for another cricketer, in 2022.

"Bailout" is the sixteenth episode in the fifth season of the NBC television series Parks and Recreation. The episode's main plotline revolves around Leslie trying to save a failing Pawnee Video Store, while Ron condemns it as meddlesome bailout politics with predictable unintended consequences. The shop pivots to porn, and Brandi Maxxxx makes a porn parody on the Government Bailout of the Video Store titled, "X," playing Leslie Knope in it. ID the porn parody title, X, which is a play on a term that was prominent in public discourse following the 2008 financial crisis. (4-word Title)

In 2023, X shot a music video inside a Brooklyn Catholic church. The video received backlash for being provocative in its imagery (The video begins with the image of a coffin that reads "R.I.P. b*tch"), prompting the parish priest's removal from administrative duties after an investigation. The investigation also led to uncovering misuse of church funds. As per a viral fan theory, the controversy's spotlight and mounting scrutiny also led to the New York mayor's indictment and exit. ID X, who as per fans, played a part in Zohran Mamdani's eventual Mayoral win.

X was an Indian poet, writer, and playwright, considered the father of modern Hindi literature and theatre. He has been described as 'Yug Charan' for his writings depicting the exploitative nature of the British Raj and for voicing the nationalistic aspirations of the country in the 19th century. His most recognized work is the play, Andher Nagari, a political satire that has been translated and performed in multiple Indian languages. Honouring his legacy, X Awards were established in 1983 by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to encourage creative writing in Hindi. ID X.

X is a port city, and home to the longest uninterrupted naturally occurring sea beach in the world. The name of the place comes from an 18th-century East India Company officer who was tasked with rehabilitating displaced communities in the region. Following his death in 1799, a commemorative marketplace was set up in the area that eventually became the name of the city. ID X.

X was a noted patron of arts and letters, convening Sanskrit-Persian scholars and painters at court. In 1655, X authored Majma-ul-Bahrain ("Confluence of the Two Seas") to explore common ground between Sufi and Vedantic thought. X also supervised the Persian rendering of roughly fifty Upanishads as Sirr-i-Akbar ("The Great Secret"), in 1657. In 2020, X's grave was finally discovered among unmarked burials in Humayun's Tomb, Delhi. ID X.

"The People vs X" is a 1996 American biographical drama film, directed by Milos Forman, with Woody Harrelson playing the role of X. The film chronicles the rise of X and his subsequent clash with religious institutions and the law. The film was critically acclaimed and earned a Best Actor nomination for Harrelson and Best Director nomination for Forman at the 69th Academy Awards. The film is based on the Supreme Court case of Y v. Falwell, a real life court battle between Reverend Jerry Falwell and X. ID X, and his creation Y.

In the 1993 season finale of Star Trek: The Next Generation, a holodeck poker game pairs Data with holographic Sir Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein (portrayed by actors), and X (playing himself). Below is an exchange from the episode: "All the quantum fluctuations in the universe will not change the cards in your hand." - Albert Einstein to X, incorrectly calling a bluff. "Wrong again, Albert." - X responds, showing his winning hand. ID X.
